extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, stakeholder organizations, industry participants, and regulated entities interested in CFPB rulemaking and opportunities to submit public comments
extracted.subtask_description: A CFPB web page listing rulemakings the Bureau is developing, describing types of rulemaking documents, and pointing readers to where they can find and submit notices and comments. It summarizes the function of proposed rules, advance notices, and other public-request mechanisms used to gather input prior to final rule issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-final rule public notice and explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: Before issuing a final rule, the CFPB generally announces and explains its proposals to address an issue and invites public comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statement describes the Bureau’s ordinary procedural practice: the Bureau will publicly announce and explain proposed actions and solicit public comments prior to issuing a final rule. The page also directs users to the comprehensive “Notice and Opportunities for Comment” page to find all notices requesting public comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed Rule
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed rule announces and explains the Bureau’s proposal to address an issue and invites the public to comment. The proposed rule and the public comments received on it form the basis of the final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a proposed rule when the Bureau intends to present a concrete regulatory proposal and formally solicit comment; comments submitted on the NPRM are part of the administrative record that informs the final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (ANPRM)
rubrics_metrics.description: An optional early step in CFPB rulemaking. Used to get initial public input on certain key aspects of potential rulemakings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ANPRMs are employed to gather early, broad input on important design questions or policy alternatives before the Bureau drafts a specific proposed rule. They are optional and serve to inform whether and how to proceed with a formal proposed rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for comment or information
rubrics_metrics.description: Label used on entries where the Bureau is soliciting public comment or information (e.g., 'Request for comment or information' shown alongside certain rule entries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These notices indicate the Bureau seeks written input or information from the public on specific topics to inform potential regulatory action. They can appear independently or in conjunction with proposed rules or ANPRMs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Call for evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Tag used on multiple entries indicating the Bureau is seeking evidence (data, studies, factual information) related to the topic to inform rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls for evidence signal a targeted request for empirical information that will help the Bureau assess problems, impacts, and policy options; they often accompany ANPRMs or early-stage rulemaking activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive Notice and Opportunities for Comment (reference)
rubrics_metrics.description: A referenced resource where users can find all notices requesting public comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page directs readers to consult the comprehensive 'Notice and Opportunities for Comment' page to browse all active and archived opportunities to submit comments and information across CFPB rulemaking activities.
